title: World fingerprints stay fixed
plain: The test builds 100 worlds and checks each against a fingerprint saved in the repo. If a world ever changes by one block, it fails.
why: A route is only the fastest for a world that never changes under it.

title: No shaky ingredients in worlds
plain: The test scans the world-building code and fails if it finds hash maps (which shuffle their order) or decimal numbers (which round differently on different machines).
why: If the world could differ between computers, a saved route would stop working.
done_when: The scan finds zero banned words.

title: Fast and slow builds agree
plain: The same 100 worlds are built in the optimised build and must match the same saved fingerprints as the debug build.
why: A route found with the fast build must still work in the checked build.
done_when: The release run matches all 100 fingerprints.

title: Corner touching is counted right
plain: Small hand-drawn maps where floor squares meet only at a corner. Floor must count them as two separate islands, and walls must count them as joined.
why: Count islands and loops wrongly and the planner sees roads that are not there or misses real ones.
done_when: Every hand-drawn shape gives its known island and loop counts.

title: Two ways to count loops agree
plain: Loops are counted by measuring holes and again by counting dots, lines and squares. A gap touching the map edge must not be counted as a loop.
why: A green test that compares a method with itself proves nothing; two different methods can disagree.
done_when: Both counts match on 100 worlds and on edge cases.

title: Sealed caves counted once
plain: A solid block with a sealed air bubble must give exactly one enclosed cave; an open bubble gives zero.
why: Sealed caves are the places a speedrunner can only reach by mining, so they must be found correctly.
done_when: Sealed bubble gives 1, open bubble gives 0, in all test shapes.

title: Placing a block can split land
plain: Placing a block on a narrow bridge must cut one island into two, and the fast update must say so.
why: Plans that place blocks need counts that can go up as well as down.
done_when: The island count rises by one and equals a full recount.

title: Random edits never drift
plain: Thousands of random mine and place steps on many worlds. After each step the quick answer must equal a full recount, and undoing must restore the old numbers.
why: One wrong step would quietly poison every later step of a plan.
done_when: Zero mismatches in every step on 100 worlds.

title: Quick update is really quick
plain: A counter records how many cells the quick update visits. One edit on a big map must visit only a small fraction of it.
why: If the quick update secretly recounts everything, planning with thousands of edits is too slow.
done_when: The visited share stays under the set limit.

title: The rival planner is fair
plain: The rival planner, given plenty of time, must find the best route on small worlds. Both planners also share one budget value and one seed list.
why: A win against a crippled rival means nothing.
done_when: The rival matches the true best route with a big budget.

title: Routes obey the game rules
plain: Every route is replayed step by step by a separate rule checker. A route through a wall that needs a pickaxe must be rejected unless the pickaxe is made first.
why: A path that looks fine on the map but breaks a game rule is not a speedrun.
done_when: Every route passes the rule checker and the trap route is rejected.

title: The truth check counts everything
plain: On a world where crafting a tool first is faster, the ground-truth search must track what you carry, and its time must equal the simulator's tick count.
why: The ground truth must not share the solver's mistakes.
done_when: The answer matches the simulator tick for tick.

title: Ties always break the same way
plain: A map with many equally fast routes is solved with the cell order shuffled. The chosen route must be identical every time.
why: Same seed, same route is a promise of the whole project.
done_when: Every shuffle gives the identical route.

title: Website stays on this computer
plain: The test starts the site and checks it only answers on your own machine's address, not on the network.
why: The site shows work in progress and should not be open to others.

title: Status cannot lie green
plain: One test is made to fail on purpose; the website must show that goal as not done.
why: A status page that is green by default hides broken work.
done_when: The failing goal shows as not done and a passing one as done.
